description: Grupo formado por estudiantes de TUMO durante el space apps challenge.
summary:
LUNAR 67 is an educational video game that we developed to play in a web browser. It is about a mission on the Moon, where the player has to take care of the crew and manage important resources such as oxygen, energy, and food. The player also has to make decisions, overcome different challenges, and build a lunar base to survive.
Our project aims to show some of the problems that could happen when trying to live on the Moon and how they can be solved. One of the main ideas is to use the resources available there instead of depending completely on supplies from Earth.
We think this project is important because it allows us to learn about space exploration in a fun way and understand why technology, planning, and teamwork are essential for future space missions.
details:
LUNAR 67 is an educational space survival video game that runs in a web browser. The player must survive for seven days in a lunar base called Selene-3 and prepare a landing platform for the rescue spacecraft. Different situations appear each day, and the player must choose what to do. These decisions have consequences and affect four resources: oxygen, food, energy, and health. They also influence the construction progress and the ending of the story. There are different endings depending on the decisions made during the mission.

The main benefit is learning about lunar exploration in an entertaining and interactive way. We want players to understand the importance of managing resources, solving problems, and thinking before making decisions.

To develop the game, we used HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and JSON. We did not use special hardware or external frameworks. The design combines a space atmosphere with indicators, animations, and an interface that allows players to follow the mission's progress.

The creativity of the project lies in turning the challenges of a lunar mission into a game where every choice can change the outcome. We considered survival, limited resources, the characteristics of the lunar environment, and scientific concepts based on NASA information. We also wanted the game to be easy to understand and use.
dataRefs: A Few Things Artemis Will Teach Us About Living and Working on the Moon
